_about: Railway gauge (release 2, batch 3; Brian's yes of 27 November 2026 17:10Z; the design director's rulings of 17:15Z and 17:48Z on r2-three-ideas/FORM-rails-rivers-1127.md, part A, and of 28 November 01:12Z). Behind the grand campaign's flag 'gauge', OFF until its gate. 'home' is the gauge a nation's trains run on, by the nation; every nation not listed runs on the standard gauge. 'relay' is how many provinces of captured track a nation's railway troops re-lay a month: a capacity, the same for every nation. A nation's trains run only on track of its own gauge.
_track: The track's gauge is a fact of the ground (the design director, 28 November 01:12Z, (4), and 01:42Z, 2): at each start, the rows of 'track' by province, read by the one start-key reader (startKey, the start rows form of 19:15Z: the exact start '1', '5', '17' or '29', from openFrom or the first day; never the latest start at or before a day). A province with no row at the start is standard. A start with no key has no table, and the switch is refused there. After the start, whatever a nation's railway troops last re-laid there (flag 'ga:<id>'), and whoever takes it next finds that gauge; the owner of a province never changes its track.
_owed: PLACEHOLDERS, named as such and never to be read as figures. The 'track' rows are filled from the owner's home gauge on each start day the door offers (turns 1, 5, 17, 29; both charts, read from the starts on 28 November); the historian's table by province replaces them, with its sources. The historian's table and the relay pace (provinces a month, for example the German conversion of 1941 and the Soviet one of 1944) were asked 17:26Z 27 November and are still owed. Until both are in, no gate runs on these figures and the switch stays off.
